projects.title: ExamGuard
projects.tagline: Examination management & identity verification for secure exam entry
projects.summary: Connects student registration, hall tickets, seating plans, invigilation, and browser-based identity verification into one auditable examination workflow. Algorithms score liveness and facial likeness while human review retains decision sovereignty.
projects.problem: Traditional exam entry relies on manual hall-ticket checks and visual ID verification by invigilators, which is slow, vulnerable to impersonation by proxy candidates, and produces no auditable trail.
howItWorks: Next.js operational dashboard manages exam schedules, hall-ticket issuance, and room-level seat allocations.
Python/FastAPI verification service receives webcam streams and runs the UniFace facial recognition pipeline with liveness estimation.
Configurable threshold rules flag potential mismatches, poor lighting, or proxy candidates for coordinator review.
Cloudinary securely stores photo evidence while PostgreSQL records an immutable audit log of all verification decisions.
highlights: Separated algorithmic verification evidence generation from final review authority — algorithms score, but humans decide.
2,554 backend tests verifying role permissions, token validations, ticket checks, and seating constraint algorithms.
Protected server-side facial embedding storage to prevent unauthorized biometric extraction.
Deterministic mock testing for webcam video capture and liveness detection fallbacks.

projects.title: SubstiFlow
projects.tagline: Offline timetable generation & faculty substitution management
projects.summary: Replaces spreadsheet-driven substitution chaos with a local desktop workflow: draft timetables, validate hard constraints, review deterministic substitute recommendations, and issue revised schedules without mutating master records.
projects.problem: Department coordinators face morning scrambles when faculty call in sick. Manual timetable spreadsheets cause classroom double-bookings, workload violations, and untracked substitution histories.
howItWorks: Electron desktop app with React and TypeScript provides a fast, offline-capable coordinator interface.
Deterministic constraint-satisfaction engine evaluates schedule availability, subject qualifications, and teaching hour caps.
Transactional SQLite database records substitutions as deltas against the immutable master schedule.
Atomic export pipeline generates formatted daily substitution slips and PDF schedules.
highlights: Local-first architecture ensures coordinators can resolve emergencies even during campus network outages.
Comprehensive property-based tests in Vitest validating constraint solver edge cases and cyclical conflicts.
Transactional SQLite rollback verification ensuring schedule mutations are never half-applied.
Immutable schedule locking once coordinator approval is granted.

projects.title: Anomoly Chat
projects.tagline: Accountless peer-to-peer chat & document transfer between browsers
projects.summary: Creates temporary browser-to-browser rooms using WebRTC data channels. Messages and documents stay in memory, binary transfers are checked with SHA-256, and sessions self-destruct on schedule without database persistence.
projects.problem: Standard messaging apps require phone numbers or email logins, persist full message histories on centralized servers, and subject private file transfers to cloud indexing.
howItWorks: PeerJS coordinates room signaling to establish direct WebRTC RTCDataChannel connections between browsers.
Ephemeral in-memory buffers handle message delivery with zero central server storage.
Files up to 10 MiB are sliced into 16 KiB binary chunks and streamed peer-to-peer with transfer progress tracking.
Client-side Web Crypto API calculates SHA-256 digests on both sender and receiver to verify payload integrity.
highlights: Accountless by design: No database, no user accounts, no message history persisted on any central server.
Scheduled session self-destruction clears all in-memory buffers upon room timer expiry.
Simulated packet-loss and reconnection test scenarios over high-latency peer connections.
Transparent security disclosures outlining WebRTC peer IP exposure boundaries.

projects.title: What's Not Up
projects.tagline: Local visual privacy controls for WhatsApp Web & Instagram
projects.summary: A Manifest V3 extension that visually obscures sensitive content already rendered in messaging web apps. Features layered DOM detection, independent privacy categories, and instant panic controls.
projects.problem: Using web messaging in public libraries, classrooms, or open-plan offices leaves private messages, sender identities, and media exposed to shoulder surfing.
howItWorks: Dynamic MutationObservers monitor chat containers for incoming messages, infinite scrolls, and tab changes.
Scoped CSS blur filters obfuscate targeted DOM elements according to user privacy preferences.
Hover-intent triggers unblur specific elements cleanly and re-engages blur immediately upon pointer exit.
Global panic-lock shortcut instantly re-engages maximum obfuscation across all active tabs.
highlights: Independent toggle categories for message bodies, contact names, profile pictures, and media previews.
Zero external network telemetry: Manifest V3 declared with minimal permissions and no remote network calls.
DOM mutation stress tests across rapid infinite-scrolling WhatsApp Web conversations.
Permission audit verifying zero access outside supported messaging origins.

projects.title: DSCASC AI
projects.tagline: Explainable NLP assistant for student guidance & campus services
projects.summary: An academic guidance assistant built around an explainable NLP pipeline: normalizes student queries, builds TF-IDF vector models, ranks with cosine similarity, and falls back gracefully below confidence thresholds.
projects.problem: College students and prospective applicants frequently struggle to locate official guidance on admissions, fees, syllabus, and placement schedules across dispersed circulars and PDF notices.
howItWorks: Text preprocessing pipeline normalizes college jargon, course abbreviations (BCA, MCA, MBA), and common student typos.
Vector engine generates TF-IDF representations from curated institutional knowledge bases.
Cosine similarity rankings identify the closest official responses with inspectable confidence scores.
Queries falling below a 0.45 similarity threshold gracefully trigger structured contact cards rather than guessing answers.
highlights: Deterministic explainability: Vector scores and similarity rankings are fully inspectable, eliminating LLM hallucinations.
Zero recurring inference costs: Runs entirely client/server-side without external paid API keys.
Comprehensive intent-matching test matrix covering 40+ curated academic categories.
Typo resilience test suite verifying query resolution across misspelled student prompts.

projects.title: ReleaseLens
projects.tagline: Continuous quality engineering & release auditing platform
projects.summary: A continuous quality engineering and product auditing platform combining automated functional testing, accessibility checks, and performance auditing into evidence-based release reports.
projects.problem: Engineering teams struggle to gather unified regression evidence, accessibility conformance, and release readiness across fragmented test outputs.
howItWorks: Automated audit runner executing functional checks, WCAG compliance tests, and API validation.
Evidence collector compiling test traces, failure screenshots, and regression metrics into structured release logs.
highlights: Evidence-based reporting for QA and release managers.
Deterministic regression tracking across builds.
